The excursion begins in central Santiago, at La Moneda government palace. Built as the royal mint in the late 18th century, the palace later became the seat of Chile's government.

Next, you will visit Plaza de Armas, the city's main historic square. Here stand buildings identified in the itinerary as the Chilean Governors' House, City Hall, Central Post Office and Royal Audience, as well as the Metropolitan Cathedral.

Santa Lucía Hill offers a panoramic view of the capital. After ascending the hill, the route continues through the modern districts of Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia, alongside the Mapocho River and Santiago's main avenues.

The group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide is included in the tour. A trip to wineries in the Maipo Valley with wine tasting is offered separately.

The square and its surroundings contain important historic buildings of Santiago: the Chilean Governors' House, City Hall, Central Post Office, the former Royal Audience building and the Metropolitan Cathedral. You will then ascend San Cristóbal Hill, which offers spectacular panoramic views over Santiago and the Andes. The tour concludes with an introduction to the city's modern districts — Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia. These prestigious neighbourhoods are known for contemporary architecture, business centres, stylish restaurants, shops and well-maintained residential areas.
